claim: VGLUT1 KO neurons display higher exchange rates of Syb2EGFP with the axonal compartment compared to wild-type neurons.
source: Through FRAP (fluorescence recovery after photo-bleaching) of boutons we measured higher exchange rates of Syb2EGFP with the axonal compartment, for VGLUT1 KO neurons compared to wild-type neurons (Figure 1B,C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C and Supplementary file 1.

claim: A higher exchange rate of VGLUT1 KO SVs with the axonal super-pool is in line with previous findings.
source: A higher exchange rate of VGLUT1 KO SVs with the axonal super-pool is in line with our previous findings (Siksou et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim references a previous publication (Siksou et al., 2013) as supporting evidence.

claim: VGLUT1 overexpression reduces SV exchange with axonal pools compared to rescue of the knock-out to endogenous levels.
source: FRAP of VGLUT1venus fluorescence revealed that VGLUT1 overexpression further reduces SV exchange with axonal pools compared to the rescue of the knock-out to endogenous levels (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: VGLUT2venus expression did not reduce the VGLUT1 KO larger super-pool phenotype.
source: Finally, VGLUT2venus expression didn't reduce the VGLUT1 KO larger super-pool phenotype (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1.

claim: VGLUT1 expression in neurons reduces the size of the SV super-pool in a dose dependent manner.
source: Therefore, VGLUT1 expression in neurons reduces the size of the SV super-pool in a dose dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of FRAP experiments showing different effects at different VGLUT1 expression levels.

claim: VGLUT1 contains 12 trans-membrane domains with both termini on the cytoplasmic side and N-glycosylation on the first luminal loop.
source: VGLUT1 contains 12 trans-membrane domains with both termini on the cytoplasmic side and N-glycosylation on the first luminal loop (Almqvist et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Almqvist et al., 2007.

claim: A triple point mutant R80Q, R176K, R314Q produces a glutamate transport deficient transporter.
source: A triple point mutant R80Q, R176K, R314Q was generated to produce a glutamate transport deficient transporter as previously reported for VGLUT2 (Herman et al., 2014; Almqvist et al., 2007, sVGLUT1 for silent VGLUT1; Figure 2A blue residues; Juge et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Herman et al., 2014, Almqvist et al., 2007, and Juge et al., 2006.

claim: Mammalian VGLUT1 displays a unique double proline-rich (PRD1 530–540; PRD2 550–556) pattern conserved in all mammals and absent in VGLUT2 and −3 or in invertebrate orthologs of VGLUT1.
source: Indeed, mammalian VGLUT1 displays a unique double proline-rich (PRD1 530–540; PRD2 550–556) pattern conserved in all mammals and absent in VGLUT2 and −3 or in invertebrate orthologs of VGLUT1 (Vinatier et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Vinatier et al., 2006.

claim: A conserved 540SYGAT sequence between PRD1 and PRD2 is present in all VGLUT isoforms including invertebrates.
source: A conserved 540SYGAT sequence between PRD1 and PRD2 is present in all VGLUT isoforms including invertebrates (Vinatier et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Vinatier et al., 2006.

claim: None of the mutants displayed a significant qualitative or quantitative difference in expression compared to wild-type controls.
source: None of the mutants displayed a significant qualitative or quantitative difference in expression compared to wild-type controls.
evidence: The claim is supported by expression level monitoring data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: Both VGLUT1mCherry and sVGLUT1mCherry rescue conditions lowered the exchange of SVs compared to VGLUT1 KO synapses significantly and to the same degree.
source: Both rescue conditions lowered the exchange of SVs compared to VGLUT1 KO synapses of the same cultures significantly and to the same degree (Figure 3B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: A remaining spontaneous activity in the knock-out cultures can be attributed to a minor but significant expression of VGLUT2 in hippocampal neurons.
source: In patch clamp experiments, a remaining spontaneous activity was found in the knock-out cultures that can be attributed to a minor but significant expression of VGLUT2 in hippocampal neurons (Wojcik et al., 2004; Miyazaki et al., 2003; Herzog et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wojcik et al., 2004, Miyazaki et al., 2003, and Herzog et al., 2006.

claim: The lower plateau of VGLUT2 expression is reached between DIV17 and DIV22.
source: To minimize this contribution we monitored VGLUT2 levels in the culture at several ages and established that the lower plateau is reached between DIV17 and DIV22 when we performed our imaging and patch clamp experiments (see Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: sVGLUT1 was unable to rescue the mEPSC amplitude to the same level as the wild type control.
source: As anticipated, sVGLUT1 was unable to rescue the mEPSC amplitude to the same level as the wild type control (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: The deficiency in the rescue of glutamate transport by sVGLUT1 is apparent in the frequency of mEPSC events, as empty SVs also cycle.
source: The deficiency in the rescue of glutamate transport by sVGLUT1 is also apparent in the frequency of mEPSC events, as empty SVs also cycle (Wojcik et al., 2004; Schuske and Jorgensen, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wojcik et al., 2004 and Schuske and Jorgensen, 2004.

claim: No impact of sVGLUT1 was seen on mIPSC features.
source: No impact of sVGLUT1 was seen on mIPSC features (Figure 3—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The triple mutation sVGLUT1 failed to rescue SV loading with glutamate, but reduced SV super-pool size to the same extent as the wild-type control.
source: Hence, the triple mutation sVGLUT1 failed to rescue SV loading with glutamate, but reduced SV super-pool size to the same extent as the wild-type control.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of FRAP and electrophysiology experiments.

claim: Only the mutations disrupting the PRD2 sequence were not able to reduce SV exchange down to WT levels.
source: In the FRAP paradigm, only the mutations disrupting the PRD2 sequence were not able to reduce SV exchange down to WT levels (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: A point mutation in PRD2 (P554A) that blocks the interaction with endophilin is sufficient to increase both the plateau of recovery and the rate of exchange of SVs.
source: A point mutation in PRD2 (P554A) that blocks the interaction with endophilin is sufficient to increase both the plateau of recovery and the rate of exchange of SVs (shorter slow half-life for P554A, Figure 4A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Time-lapse imaging confirmed a significantly larger mobile axonal super-pool of SVs for VGLUT1P554A-venus but not for VGLUT1S540A-venus compared to WT rescue.
source: This assay confirmed a significantly larger mobile axonal super-pool of SVs for VGLUT1P554A-venus but not for VGLUT1S540A-venus compared to WT rescue (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: No difference in axonal transport speed could be measured between the three constructs.
source: Yet, no difference in axonal transport speed could be measured between the three constructs (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: VGLUT1venus constructs displayed an additional slow band in PhosTag gel migration, except when samples were digested with alkaline phosphatase.
source: VGLUT1venus constructs displayed an additional slow band in PhosTag gel migration, except when samples were digested with alkaline phosphatase (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by PhosTag assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: All mutants including ∆C-term displayed the second slower band in PhosTag gel migration.
source: All mutants including ∆C-term displayed this second slower band.
evidence: The claim is supported by PhosTag assay data.

claim: VGLUT1 appears to be phosphorylated, but not at the C-terminal tail.
source: Thus, VGLUT1 appears to be phosphorylated, but not at the C-terminal tail, and the function of the extremely conserved 540-SYGAT sequence therefore remains unclear.
evidence: The claim is inferred from PhosTag assay results showing phosphorylation in all constructs including C-terminal deletions.

claim: VGLUT1P554A rescued miniature EPSC amplitudes to a similar level as the wild type transporter.
source: VGLUT1P554A rescued miniature EPSC amplitudes to a similar level as the wild type transporter (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: VGLUT1P554A increased the frequency of miniature events significantly more than the WT rescue.
source: Interestingly, VGLUT1P554A increased the frequency of miniature events significantly more than the WT rescue (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: mIPSC frequencies were similar in all three conditions (sham, WT, and VGLUT1P554A).
source: In contrast to this, mIPSC frequencies were similar in all three conditions (Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, and Supplementary file 1.

claim: VENUS fluorescence intensity at boutons was not significantly different between groups tested by electrophysiology.
source: As intended in our rescue strategy, VENUS fluorescence intensity at boutons was not significantly different between groups tested by electrophysiology (Figure 4J).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 4J.

claim: The PRD2 sequence of mammalian VGLUT1 is sufficient to reduce SV super-pool size and mEPSC frequency.
source: Therefore, the PRD2 sequence of mammalian VGLUT1 is sufficient to reduce SV super-pool size and mEPSC frequency.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of FRAP and electrophysiology experiments with PRD2 mutants.

claim: The SH3 domain of EndophilinA1 matched the sham control recovery in FRAP experiments.
source: The SH3 domain of EndophilinA1 was used to displace endogenous full-length EndophilinA1 to test the contribution of the membrane binding Bin1, Amphiphysin, RVs (BAR) domain. The FRAP curve in this experiment matched the sham control recovery (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Endo-SH3E329K,S336K shifted the FRAP recovery to a significantly higher plateau, creating a phenocopy of the VGLUT1P554A and VGLUT1 KO mutants.
source: The SH3 domain of EndophilinA1 mutated at E329K and S336K was over-expressed to displace endogenous EndophilinA1 and block the interaction with the SH3B domain of intersectin1 (Pechstein et al., 2015). Endo-SH3E329K,S336K shifted the FRAP recovery to a significantly higher plateau, creating a phenocopy of the VGLUT1P554A and VGLUT1 KO mutants (Figure 5B,C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C and Supplementary file 1, and a citation to Pechstein et al., 2015.

claim: The SH3B domain of intersectin1 shifted the FRAP recovery to a higher plateau.
source: Similarly, the SH3B domain of intersectin1 was over-expressed to displace endogenous intersectin1 from EndophilinA1. ITSN1-SH3B also shifted the FRAP recovery to a higher plateau.
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Full length intersectin1 may be required for the VGLUT1 mediated reduction of SV super pool.
source: Hence, full length intersectin1 may be required for the VGLUT1 mediated reduction of SV super pool (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the FRAP experimental results with ITSN1-SH3B overexpression.

claim: Competition experiments reveal the involvement of EndophilinA1 and intersectin1 in a complex with VGLUT1 in the negative regulation of SV super pool size in mammals.
source: Taken together, these competition experiments reveal the involvement of EndophilinA1 and interectin1 in a complex with VGLUT1 in the negative regulation of SV super pool size in mammals.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of competition experiments with SH3 domains.

claim: VGLUT1 PRD2 motif is a negative regulator of SV mobility and mEPSC frequency.
source: In the present study we could observe that VGLUT1 PRD2 motif is a negative regulator of SV mobility and mEPSC frequency.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of FRAP and electrophysiology experiments.

claim: SV super-pool reduction is mediated by an interaction of endophilinA1 with both VGLUT1 PRD2 and intersectin1 SH3B domains.
source: Our data support that SV super-pool reduction is mediated by an interaction of endophilinA1 with both VGLUT1 PRD2 and intersectin1 SH3B domains.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of competition experiments.

claim: Several dileucine-like motifs are involved in VGLUT1 endocytosis.
source: Previous works had shown that several dileucine-like motifs are involved in VGLUT1 endocytosis (Voglmaier et al., 2006; Pan et al., 2015; Foss et al., 2013) and that the PRD2 of VGLUT1 regulates endocytosis during long trains of stimulation (Voglmaier et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Voglmaier et al., 2006, Pan et al., 2015, and Foss et al., 2013.

claim: The PRD2 of VGLUT1 regulates endocytosis during long trains of stimulation.
source: Previous works had shown that several dileucine-like motifs are involved in VGLUT1 endocytosis (Voglmaier et al., 2006; Pan et al., 2015; Foss et al., 2013) and that the PRD2 of VGLUT1 regulates endocytosis during long trains of stimulation (Voglmaier et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Voglmaier et al., 2006.

claim: The present data provide the first molecular separation of glutamate transport and SV trafficking functions of VGLUT1.
source: The present data provide the first molecular separation of glutamate transport and SV trafficking functions of VGLUT1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the results with sVGLUT1 mutant showing separation of transport and trafficking functions.

claim: The sVGLUT1 mutant allowed testing the function of the VGLUT1 backbone structure without potential interference brought by the complex flow of ions occurring through glutamate loading.
source: The sVGLUT1 mutant allowed us to test the function of the VGLUT1 backbone structure without potential interference brought by the complex flow of ions occurring through glutamate loading (Schenck et al., 2009; Preobraschenski et al., 2014; Eriksen et al., 2016; Juge et al., 2006; Goh et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schenck et al., 2009, Preobraschenski et al., 2014, Eriksen et al., 2016, Juge et al., 2006, and Goh et al., 2011.

claim: sVGLUT1 revealed that glutamate transport is not related to the negative regulation of SV super-pool size.
source: sVGLUT1 revealed that glutamate transport is not related to the negative regulation of SV super-pool size.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the results showing that sVGLUT1 reduces super-pool size despite lacking transport function.

claim: The C-terminal proline-rich domain PRD2 supports the negative regulation of SV mobility and mEPSC frequency in mammals.
source: Hence, distinctively from the dileucine based endocytosis of VGLUTs, the C-terminal proline-rich domain PRD2 supports the negative regulation of SV mobility and mEPSC frequency in mammals.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of experiments with PRD2 mutants.

claim: SV mobility inhibition is operated independently of glutamate loading processed by the core trans-membrane domains.
source: SV mobility inhibition is operated independently of glutamate loading processed by the core trans-membrane domains.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the results with sVGLUT1 mutant.

claim: Synaptic vesicles are segregated from other organelles in the nerve terminal, and grouped in a cluster.
source: Synaptic vesicles are segregated from other organelles in the nerve terminal, and grouped in a cluster (Gray, 1959).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gray, 1959.

claim: It has been proposed that SVs are recruited to the cluster by synapsins to an actin based cytoskeleton.
source: It has been proposed that SVs are recruited to the cluster by synapsins to an actin based cytoskeleton (Hilfiker et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hilfiker et al., 1999.

claim: Several lines of evidence suggest a different mechanism involving the low affinity binding of many partners forming a liquid phase separation to the rest of the cytosol.
source: Yet, several lines of evidence suggest a different mechanism involving the low affinity binding of many partners forming a liquid phase separation to the rest of the cytosol (Milovanovic and De Camilli, 2017; Pechstein and Shupliakov, 2010; Sankaranarayanan et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Milovanovic and De Camilli, 2017, Pechstein and Shupliakov, 2010, and Sankaranarayanan et al., 2003.

claim: EndophilinA1, intersectin, amphiphysin are abundant within the vesicle cluster.
source: Indeed, endophilinA1, intersectin, amphiphysin are abundant within the vesicle cluster (Figure 5—figure supplement 1; Pechstein and Shupliakov, 2010; Evergren et al., 2007) while the binding of SH3 domains to proline-rich motifs has been shown to generate liquid phase separations in a synthetic assay (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and citations to Pechstein and Shupliakov, 2010 and Evergren et al., 2007.

claim: The binding of SH3 domains to proline-rich motifs has been shown to generate liquid phase separations in a synthetic assay.
source: Indeed, endophilinA1, intersectin, amphiphysin are abundant within the vesicle cluster (Figure 5—figure supplement 1; Pechstein and Shupliakov, 2010; Evergren et al., 2007) while the binding of SH3 domains to proline-rich motifs has been shown to generate liquid phase separations in a synthetic assay (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2012.

claim: Synapsins were recently shown to induce liquid phase separation with lipid vesicles.
source: Further, synapsins were recently shown to induce liquid phase separation with lipid vesicles (Milovanovic et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Milovanovic et al., 2018.

claim: The best model to date infers the liquid phase separation of SVs in a dynamic array of labile interactions between synapsins, dephosphins (endophilins, amphiphysins, EPS15, synaptojanins…) and intersectins.
source: Hence, the best model to date infers the liquid phase separation of SVs in a dynamic array of labile interactions between synapsins, dephosphins (endophilins, amphiphysins, EPS15, synaptojanins…) and intersectins.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the cited literature on liquid phase separation and SV clustering.

claim: A slower re-acidification of PRD2 deleted VGLUT1-phluorin probes during long trains of stimulation suggested that the recruitment of endophilinA1 increases the endocytosis efficiency of VGLUT1 SVs.
source: Previously, a slower re-acidification of PRD2 deleted VGLUT1-phluorin probes during long trains of stimulation suggested that the recruitment of endophilinA1 increases the endocytosis efficiency of VGLUT1 SVs (Voglmaier et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Voglmaier et al., 2006.

claim: Recent reports indicate that endophilinA1 interaction with intersectin1 favors clathrin uncoating.
source: However, recent reports indicate that endophilinA1 interaction with intersectin1 favors clathrin uncoating (Pechstein et al., 2015; Milosevic et al., 2011), whereas the clathrin coat was shown to inhibit SV acidification (Farsi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pechstein et al., 2015 and Milosevic et al., 2011.

claim: The clathrin coat was shown to inhibit SV acidification.
source: However, recent reports indicate that endophilinA1 interaction with intersectin1 favors clathrin uncoating (Pechstein et al., 2015; Milosevic et al., 2011), whereas the clathrin coat was shown to inhibit SV acidification (Farsi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Farsi et al., 2018.

claim: The recruitment of endophilinA1 and intersectin1 at SVs may speed up clathrin uncoating and SV acidification.
source: Therefore, the recruitment of endophilinA1 and intersectin1 at SVs may speed up clathrin uncoating and SV acidification.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the cited literature on endophilinA1/intersectin1 function and clathrin uncoating.

claim: Intersectin1 (ITSN1) SH3B was shown to interact with the SH3 domain of endophilinA1 while preserving the interaction of endophilinA1 with its PRD targets on Dynamin and VGLUT1.
source: More recently, intersectin1 (ITSN1) SH3B was shown to interact with the SH3 domain of endophilinA1 while preserving the interaction of endophilinA1 with its PRD targets on Dynamin and VGLUT1 (Pechstein et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pechstein et al., 2015.

claim: Intersectin1 may interact directly with VGLUT1 through the SH3A domain.
source: Furthermore, intersectin1 may as well interact directly with VGLUT1 through the SH3A domain (Santos et al., 2014; Richter et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Santos et al., 2014 and Richter et al., 2018.

claim: The present data provide evidence for a reduction of the SV super-pool size to the benefit of the SV clusters mediated by a tripartite complex between VGLUT1 PRD2, endophilinA1 and intersectin1.
source: Our present data provide evidence for a reduction of the SV super-pool size to the benefit of the SV clusters mediated by a tripartite complex between VGLUT1 PRD2, endophilinA1 and intersectin1 (VGLUT1/EndoA1/ITSN1, Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of competition experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: The increase in SV exchange rate when PRD2 is mutated strongly suggests a reduced strength in the interactions scavenging SVs in the cluster.
source: The increase in SV exchange rate when PRD2 is mutated strongly suggests a reduced strength in the interactions scavenging SVs in the cluster (Staras et al., 2010; Herzog et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the FRAP results and supported by citations to Staras et al., 2010 and Herzog et al., 2011.

claim: The present data fit well with recent reports of intersectin1 function in the re-clustering of newly endocytosed SVs, and on the nano-scale organization of synapsins at terminals.
source: Our data also fit well with recent reports of intersectin1 function in the re-clustering of newly endocytosed SVs, and on the nano-scale organization of synapsins at terminals (Gerth et al., 2017; Winther et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gerth et al., 2017 and Winther et al., 2015.

claim: Downstream of VGLUT1/EndoA1/ITSN1, the SV super-pool reduction may be driven by interactions of intersectin1 with synapsins and/or through remodeling of the actin cytoskeleton surrounding the cluster.
source: Downstream of VGLUT1/EndoA1/ITSN1, the SV super-pool reduction may be driven by interactions of intersectin1 with synapsins (Milovanovic et al., 2018; Winther et al., 2015) and/or through remodeling of the actin cytoskeleton surrounding the cluster (Humphries et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is speculative and supported by citations to Milovanovic et al., 2018, Winther et al., 2015, and Humphries et al., 2014.

claim: Vesicular glutamate transporters are necessary and sufficient to generate a glutamatergic phenotype in neurons by loading secretory organelles with glutamate.
source: Vesicular glutamate transporters are necessary and sufficient to generate a glutamatergic phenotype in neurons by loading secretory organelles with glutamate (Takamori et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Takamori et al., 2000.

claim: Quantal size modulation has been reported upon changes in the level of VGLUT expression.
source: Quantal size modulation has been reported upon changes in the level of VGLUT expression (Wojcik et al., 2004; Moechars et al., 2006; Wilson et al., 2005) and is reproduced in our present work (Figures 3 and 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wojcik et al., 2004, Moechars et al., 2006, and Wilson et al., 2005, and by data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: EndophilinA1 binding to the VGLUT1 PRD2 sequence was shown to reduce SV release probability.
source: Furthermore, EndophilinA1 binding to the VGLUT1 PRD2 sequence was shown to reduce SV release probability (Weston et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Weston et al., 2011.

claim: The present dataset supports the role of VGLUT1/EndoA1/ITSN1 in the reduction of mEPSC frequency and SV exchange between clusters and super-pool.
source: Our dataset now supports the role of VGLUT1/EndoA1/ITSN1 in the reduction of mEPSC frequency and SV exchange between clusters and super-pool (Figures 4 and 5).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Weston et al. did not see an effect of VGLUT1 ∆PRD2 on mEPSC frequency but only on SV release probability.
source: A discrepancy may arise from the fact that Weston et al. did not see an effect of VGLUT1 ∆PRD2 on mEPSC frequency but only on SV release probability.
evidence: The claim references findings from Weston et al. study.

claim: The autaptic culture system from Weston et al. prevents the formation of a network.
source: However, this may be explained by two differences in our recording conditions. First, the autaptic culture system from Weston et al. prevents the formation of a network.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of autaptic culture systems.

claim: mEPSCs in autaptic conditions arise from a single cell (the recorded cell), while in continental cultures they are generated by multiple cells targeting the recorded neuron.
source: Autapses are powerful tools to dissect evoked activity, but mEPSCs in autaptic conditions arise from a single cell (the recorded cell), while in continental cultures they are generated by multiple cells targeting the recorded neuron.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of autaptic versus continental culture systems.

claim: Continental cultures build a network that generates activity, which most likely leads to different set-points of SV super-pool sizes and homeostatic plasticity compared to autaptic micro-islands.
source: Additionally, continental cultures build a network that generates activity, which most likely leads to different set-points of SV super-pool sizes and homeostatic plasticity compared to autaptic micro-islands (De Gois et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is speculative and supported by a citation to De Gois et al., 2005.

claim: Weston and colleagues worked before 14 days in culture, whereas the present work was performed after 17 days in culture when VGLUT2 expression reached a lower plateau.
source: Second, Weston and colleagues worked before 14 days in culture, whereas we worked after 17 days in culture when VGLUT2 expression reached a lower plateau and may generate less background mEPSC activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Wojcik et al., 2004; Herzog et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and citations to Wojcik et al., 2004 and Herzog et al., 2006.

claim: The molecular mechanism of SV super-pool reduction requires the EndoA1 SH3 domain, but not the BAR domain.
source: The molecular mechanism of SV super-pool reduction that we uncovered requires the EndoA1 SH3 domain, but not the BAR domain (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the competition experiment results shown in Figure 5.

claim: Weston et al. (2011) showed that endophilinA1 promotes SV release probability through dimerization and BAR domain mediated membrane binding.
source: Previously, Weston et al. (2011) showed that endophilinA1 promotes SV release probability through dimerization and BAR domain mediated membrane binding.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Weston et al., 2011.

claim: The current results complement the Weston et al. model by adding a pathway through which VGLUT1/EndoA1 recruit intersectin1 to promote SV clustering and mEPSC frequency reduction in a BAR domain independent fashion.
source: Our current results complement this model by adding a pathway through which VGLUT1/EndoA1 recruit intersectin1 to promote SV clustering and mEPSC frequency reduction in a BAR domain independent fashion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of the present study.

claim: Free EndophilinA1 may actively promote SV exocytosis through membrane binding mechanisms while VGLUT1-bound EndophilinA1 may actively reduce SV mobility and exocytosis through an intersectin1 dependent pathway.
source: Hence, free EndophilinA1 may actively promote SV exocytosis through membrane binding mechanisms while VGLUT1-bound EndophilinA1 may actively reduce SV mobility and exocytosis through an intersectin1 dependent pathway.
evidence: The claim is a speculative model inferred from the combined results.

claim: Beyond setting the quantal size, VGLUT1 influences glutamate release parameters most likely by changing the strength of SVs phase separation in clusters.
source: Beyond setting the quantal size, VGLUT1 influences glutamate release parameters most likely by changing the strength of SVs phase separation in clusters.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of the study.

claim: Neuromodulation has been very recently proposed to tune SV pools in the axon through GPCR signaling and synapsin phosphorylation.
source: In this line, neuromodulation has been very recently proposed to tune SV pools in the axon through GPCR signaling and synapsin phosphorylation (Patzke et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Patzke et al., 2019.

claim: Glutamate secretion at excitatory synapses is tightly regulated to allow for the precise tuning of synaptic strength.
source: Glutamate secretion at excitatory synapses is tightly regulated to allow for the precise tuning of synaptic strength.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Vesicular Glutamate Transporters (VGLUT) accumulate glutamate into synaptic vesicles (SV) and thereby regulate quantal size.
source: Vesicular Glutamate Transporters (VGLUT) accumulate glutamate into synaptic vesicles (SV) and thereby regulate quantal size.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The number of release sites and the release probability of SVs may be regulated by the organization of active-zone proteins and SV clusters.
source: Further, the number of release sites and the release probability of SVs maybe regulated by the organization of active-zone proteins and SV clusters.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The present work uncovers a mechanism mediating an increased SV clustering through the interaction of VGLUT1 second proline-rich domain, endophilinA1 and intersectin1.
source: In the present work, we uncover a mechanism mediating an increased SV clustering through the interaction of VGLUT1 second proline-rich domain, endophilinA1 and intersectin1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of the study.

claim: The strengthening of SV clusters results in a combined reduction of axonal SV super-pool size and miniature excitatory events frequency.
